In the instant case the prosecution is alleging that the accused person being the driver of the BMTC bus drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and caused accident due to which the victim sustained grievous injuries and prosecution contended that accused committed the offences punishable U/s.279 and 338 of IPC.

Section 279 IPC deals with rash and negligent driving of any vehicle or riding on a public way in a rash C.C.No.8942/2022 and negligent manner so as to endanger human life or likely to cause hurt or injury to any person.

In order to constitute an offence U/s.279 of IPC, it must be established that the accused being the driver driven vehicle negligently and ran his bus over road humps due to which the passenger inside the bus sustained injuries on his spinal card.

The prosecution has to establish that accused was the driver of the bus who was driving the bus on a public way and in similar manner he has drove the bus in rash and negligent manner to Jayanagara Trps vs Shanakargouda Patil on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126293510/

sentences.text: For the purpose of section 279 rash and negligent may be described as criminal rashness or criminal negligence.
It must be more than mere carelessness of error of judgment.

The essential ingredients of section 279 are: (1) rash and negligent driving or riding on a public way, (ii) The act must be such as to endanger human life or likely to cause hurt or injury to any person.

20. The prosecution has to establish that the accused is the person who is driving the bus on the alleged day and he negligently driven the bus in such a rash and negligent manner that the victim sustained injury due to rash driving of the accused.
Here the prosecution has burden to establish the rash and C.C.No.8942/2022 negligent act of the accused driver is the reason for the incident.

To prove that aspect the prosecution has relied on P.W.1 victim, P.W.2 and P.W.3 are the eye witnesses,
P.W.4 and 5 are the mahazar witnesses, Ex.P.6 is the Investigating officer.
21. The case of the prosecution is that the accused driver driven his bus in a negligent manner and due to which the victim sustained injuries.
The victim deposed that due to negligent driving when the bus ran over the road hump it jumped and hence he sustained injuries.
Upon perusal of the wound certificate as per Ex.P.7 all the injuries are noticed on the lower back of the complainant.
The said patient while admitting in hospital has given complete details of the accident.
Admittedly if an accident has taken place in a bus filled with passengers then several passengers of the bus might have sustained injuries.
In the case on hand apart from complainant no other person sustained injury.

Particularly if bus jumps in high speed the person will fly from the seat and his head is the first point which will get damaged or if he has fallen down his face will get damaged, but in the instant case damages is noticed on lower back.
the complainant contend that due to rash driving he sustained injuries on his lower back, with the manner accident is described the wound sustained is not C.C.No.8942/2022 probable.
Moreover if at all the said incident has taken place then the complainant might have placed relevant documents with regard to his journey.

P.W.2 he was also inmate of the bus and he has given the nubmer to injured and asked him to call, but in the instant case the incident has taken place on 08.05.2022, the complaint was lodged after 11 days i.e.,
19;05.2022.
The complainant says he has seen the name plate of the bus driver and he has note down the number of the bus.
As per his version he was unable to stand and the bus driver along with conductor shifted him to footpath of the bus shelter and left him there.
If he is not in a position to stand then how can he see bus number it is not the case of the complainant that he has ticket and based on that ticket he caame to knnow about bus number.
He cames he has monthly pass.
In the case on hand the ambulance was not called to bus stand where he was lying.
He claims he was unable to stand and called his relatives.
But the said relatives is not listed as witness.
As per his version accident has taken place near south end circle in a moving bus that too in morning hours.

If a road accident has taken place then generally the public will gather and will call for ambulance or local police and generlaly if a person scream then the passengers will alert atleast conductor of the bus, but in the case on hand no such incident has taken place he C.C.No.8942/2022 injured in south end circle junction and he all the way travelled till market bus stand it raises doubt about the genuiness of the case.
Moreover the concerned hospital staff when clearly write down admitted with a history of road accident then why they have not sent MLC Report to the concerned station.
As per the rules if any person comes to hospital with an history of road accident it is the duty of the hospital staff to intimate the same to jurisdictional police.

In the case on hand no such intimation is sent by Jayanagara Trps vs Shanakargouda Patil on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126293510/
6 hospital and they alleged complaint was lodged after a lapse of 11 days after his discharge.
22.
The prosecution examined one inmate as PW.2 the said witness in cross examination deposed he has business in Kabalahalli which is 40 KM from Bengaluru City.
He did not give satisfactory explanation why he came to Bengaluru on the said day.
Further he contended there are 15 passengers in the said bus.
If at all he has seen the incident then why he get down in the middle of the bus.
Why he has not made attempt to take him to Hospital.
Which raises doubts about his presence in the said bus.
The prosecution examined the conductor of the bus as PW3.
He deposed about existence of CCTV camera inside the bus.
Why prosecution has not made attempt to recover the same.
Further, he deposed about panic button in every seat which will alert the driver by C.C.No.8942/2022 raising alaram.
The said button was not used by the injured and witness though turned hostile and subjected to cross examination nothing worthfull is elicited from his mouth.
The presence of P.W.2 at accident spot appears to be doubtful and he does not inspire confidence.
23. The contention of the accused that they have lodged false complaint and no such incident has taken place and in order to obtain compensation they have made false allegation.
Here the burden is upon the prosecution to clear the cloud created by defence.
Prosecution contended accused drove the bus negligently and due to which the incident has taken place.

As per the version of P.W.1 and 3 after the alleged act of running over the road humps in negligent manner the bus moved forward for around 5 KM and when the injured started screaming as per the say of P.W.1 the bus was not parked by the side of the road.
Though around 15 passengers were inside the bus.
Upon perusal of the sketch map as per Ex.P.4 the alleged incident has shown on road hump and they did not mention the place where the bus was stopped or anything.

As per the narration of P.W.2 the road hump is 1ft in height and 0.5ft in width with that said height and width the alleged injury is not possible and as discussed earlier with the impact as per C.C.No.8942/2022 narration sustaining injury on lower back is not possible unless there is a history of previous injury to back portion.
Here the delay in lodging complaint and not sending MLC to local police raises doubt about the truthfullness of the case.

24. As far as other question is concerned that whether the accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of accused, it is pertinent to note that there are two eye witnesses of the accident i.e., PW.2 and 3, though they stated that the Bus was being driven in a rash and negligent manner but they have not said anything about the manner of driving by the accused.
So testimony being silent on this aspect, what was rash and negligent in the manner of driving by the accused has been completely left with the court to presume.
25. In the present case the evidence of PW1 and 2 are inconclusive to prove negligent or rash driving on the part of the accused driver, it simply proves the factum of accident.
Further, the alleged eye witness cited by the prosecution did not inspire confidence.
Admittedly, the accident took place when the Bus was full of passengers and none of the passengers had shouted to stop the Bus after accident.

26. Coming to the facts of the present case, the prosecution had to prove Rash and Negligent driving on C.C.No.8942/2022 the part of the accused for both offences u/s 279 IPC as well as 338 IPC to Jayanagara Trps vs Shanakargouda Patil on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126293510/
7 warrant conviction of the accused.
But the above discussion clearly shows that the evidence against the accused is not conclusive and the prosecution has not been able to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
Therefore, looking to the evidence available on record and the materials placed by way of oral and exhibits, the case of prosecution appears to be doubtful.
Therefore, in the circumstances of the case, as per the rules of criminal justice if any doubt arise about the commission of the act then such doubt shall be in favour of accused.
The prosecution has failed to prove the alleged offence against the accused.
Accordingly, the points under consideration are answered point No.1 to 3 IN THE NEGATIVE.
27. POINT No.4:

In view of the above discussions and findings I proceed to pass the following ORDER Acting U/sec. 255(1) of Criminal procedure code, the accused is hereby acquitted of the offences alleged against them punishable U/sec. 279 and 338 of IPC, Sec.134(a and b) R/w.187 of M.V.Act.
The bail bonds of accused and surety bonds shall stands cancelled after the appeal period.

20. The prosecution has to establish that the accused is the person who is driving the bus on the alleged day and he negligently driven the bus in such a rash and negligent manner that the victim sustained injury due to rash driving of the accused.
Here the prosecution has burden to establish the rash and C.C.No.8942/2022 negligent act of the accused driver is the reason for the incident.
21. The case of the prosecution is that the accused driver driven his bus in a negligent manner and due to which the victim sustained injuries.
As per his version he was unable to stand and the bus driver along with conductor shifted him to footpath of the bus shelter and left him there.
If a road accident has taken place then generally the public will gather and will call for ambulance or local police and generlaly if a person scream then the passengers will alert atleast conductor of the bus, but in the case on hand no such incident has taken place he C.C.No.8942/2022 injured in south end circle junction and he all the way travelled till market bus stand it raises doubt about the genuiness of the case.
Moreover the concerned hospital staff when clearly write down admitted with a history of road accident then why they have not sent MLC Report to the concerned station.
As per the rules if any person comes to hospital with an history of road accident it is the duty of the hospital staff to intimate the same to jurisdictional police.
As per the version of P.W.1 and 3 after the alleged act of running over the road humps in negligent manner the bus moved forward for around 5 KM and when the injured started screaming as per the say of P.W.1 the bus was not parked by the side of the road.
So testimony being silent on this aspect, what was rash and negligent in the manner of driving by the accused has been completely left with the court to presume.
25. In the present case the evidence of PW1 and 2 are inconclusive to prove negligent or rash driving on the part of the accused driver, it simply proves the factum of accident.
Further, the alleged eye witness cited by the prosecution did not inspire confidence.
Admittedly, the accident took place when the Bus was full of passengers and none of the passengers had shouted to stop the Bus after accident.
26. Coming to the facts of the present case, the prosecution had to prove Rash and Negligent driving on C.C.No.8942/2022 the part of the accused for both offences u/s 279 IPC as well as 338 IPC to Jayanagara Trps vs Shanakargouda Patil on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126293510/
7 warrant conviction of the accused.
But the above discussion clearly shows that the evidence against the accused is not conclusive and the prosecution has not been able to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
Therefore, looking to the evidence available on record and the materials placed by way of oral and exhibits, the case of prosecution appears to be doubtful.
Therefore, in the circumstances of the case, as per the rules of criminal justice if any doubt arise about the commission of the act then such doubt shall be in favour of accused.
The prosecution has failed to prove the alleged offence against the accused.
